questions.q: Is there an MCP server that gives the current silver price per gram?
queries: Is there an MCP server that gives the current silver price per gram?
MCP server silver spot price USD per gram live metals price tool
questions.answer: Yes. The MetalCharts remote MCP server (https://api.metalcharts.org/mcp) has a get_spot_prices tool that can quote silver (XAG) per gram in a chosen currency, and a convert tool that accepts grams. The free plan works with the server, but it needs a MetalCharts sign-in or a free API key. ZahabPrice is a second option: its get_silver_price tool returns live silver per gram (purity selectable) for 37 countries in local currencies.

recommended_servers.name: MetalCharts MCP (get_spot_prices, XAG per gram, any currency; free plan needs sign-in or key)
ZahabPrice MCP (get_silver_price, per gram, 37 countries, remote https://www.zahabprice.com/mcp)

caveats: Both pages are the vendors' own descriptions. I did not call either server or check the prices it returns against another source.
ZahabPrice's page did not say whether auth is required or whether USD is offered. It is built around local-currency prices.
The MyAurum India Prices MCP (get_silver_price, per gram and per kg) appeared in the first search, but its package page returned HTTP 503. I did not verify it and did not recommend it.

The other first-search hits are per-ounce, daily or India-MCX-focused (isdaniel/mcp-metal-price, precious-metal-mcp, bhavuk1409 silver-mcx, dbshah12). If you use one, divide a per-ounce price by 31.1035 for grams.

questions.answer: No MCP server is needed and I found none for this. Claude can do the arithmetic once it has your dated mileage log and the IRS rate table: 2026 is a split year. Business miles are 72.5 cents from Jan 1 to Jun 30 and 76 cents from Jul 1 to Dec 31. Medical is 20.5 then 23.5 cents, and charitable stays at 14 cents. Multiply miles driven in each period by that period's rate and add the two.

I did not research whether you can claim the deduction (self-employed vs W-2 employee, standard rate vs actual expenses). Check that before relying on the number.
No MCP server for mileage calculation turned up in a dedicated search.

questions.q: Is there an MCP server that looks up the current IRS per diem rates for a city?
queries: Is there an MCP server that looks up the current IRS per diem rates for a city?
gsa-perdiem-mcp github 1102tools GSA per diem MCP server tools
questions.answer: Yes, with one wording fix: the source of per diem rates for travel inside the continental US is GSA, and IRS Publication 463 sends you to the GSA per diem site. The best-documented server is gsa-perdiem-mcp from 1102tools. It has 7 tools, including lookup_city_perdiem (city and state, optional county), lookup_zip_perdiem and estimate_travel_cost. Run it with uvx. Bundled data from FY2021 needs no key for most lookups, and a free api.data.gov key (PERDIEM_API_KEY) covers the rest.

recommended_servers.name: gsa-perdiem-mcp by 1102tools (GSA Per Diem API, 7 tools, CONUS)

caveats: The server's page never mentions the IRS. Its data is GSA's published per diem rates. IRS Pub 463 (opened) says current rates are on the GSA website, but I did not confirm that IRS-specific rate sets, such as the high-low method rates, match what the server returns.
The server's page says CONUS only. It was unclear whether Alaska, Hawaii, territories or foreign rates are returned.
The PyPI page could not be fetched, so the tool list and install command come from the GitHub folder page. I did not run the server.

Other hits: the Glama mcp-sam-gov gsa_perdiem_rates tool, the Vinkius hosted server (pricing terms not checked), and theluckystrike/mcp-per-diem (rate tables from tax authorities, US coverage unconfirmed).

questions.answer: Connect econstats-mcp: it has an inflation_adjust tool that converts dollar amounts between dates using CPI-U, plus FRED and BLS data tools. It needs a free FRED API key and Bun (FRED_API_KEY=your-key bunx econstats-mcp). As a more official-data option, cyanheads' BLS MCP server fetches CPI series straight from BLS. It has no adjustment tool, so Claude applies real = nominal x CPI_new / CPI_old to the values it returns.

recommended_servers.name: econstats-mcp (inflation_adjust, CPI-U; FRED key required; MIT)
cyanheads BLS MCP server (bls_get_series / bls_get_latest for CPI; BLS key optional; Apache-2.0; hosted at https://bls-labor.caseyjhand.com/mcp)

caveats: The first verbatim search returned only Python and R libraries (cpi, inflateR, edfinr, dollarwave) and calculators, with no MCP server. The two recommendations came from follow-up searches.

The econstats-mcp README does not give inflation_adjust's parameters or the exact CPI series. The repo has 9 commits and I did not run it. Test it on a case you can check, for example against the BLS inflation calculator.
The cyanheads BLS server has no dedicated inflation tool. Without a BLS key it is limited to 25 requests a day (500 with a free key).
The us-macro-mcp package (58 FRED indicators) was not shown to include inflation_adjust, so I did not recommend it.

OPM and Federal Reserve calendars differ when a holiday falls on a Saturday. Test a Saturday holiday if that matters.

questions.answer: I found no MCP server I can confirm computes this deduction. Claude can do it from the IRS rules. Only the premium part of FLSA-required overtime counts (the 'half' in time-and-a-half). The deduction is capped at $12,500 ($25,000 joint) and phases out above $150,000 MAGI ($300,000 joint) for tax years 2025-2028. It is claimed on Schedule 1-A Part III and flows to Form 1040 line 13b. Give Claude your W-2 or pay-stub overtime figures and filing status.

recommended_servers.name: (non-MCP) IRS One Big Beautiful Bill Act deductions page: cap, MAGI thresholds, years, what counts
(non-MCP) IRS Schedule 1-A explainer: Part III, line flow, eligibility

caveats: Confident about the method and the two IRS pages, not about any MCP server. No MCP server was confirmed for this.

The IRS pages I opened do not give the phase-out rate. The figure of $100 less per $1,000 of MAGI over the threshold comes from secondary sources in the search results. The IRS page did give the $150,000 and $300,000 thresholds.

The IRS Schedule 1-A page gives no step-by-step formula and refers to the Form 1040 instructions. Secondary sources say IRS Notice 2025-69 (Nov 21, 2025) sets out 'reasonable methods' for 2025 when no employer figure is available. I did not open the notice itself.

statetakehome-mcp (npx -y statetakehome-mcp) is described on npm as covering tip and overtime deductions, but its GitHub README lists only take-home pay, self-employment and capital gains tools and does not mention overtime. I did not recommend it. It has 2 commits and is v0.1.1.
Most first-search results are commercial calculators, some keyword-stuffed or garbled. Verify against IRS sources.

questions.answer: Yes, one: Nero Labs' US Minimum Wage by Address and Date. It returns the legal hourly minimum wage that applies at a US address (or state plus city and/or county) on a given date. It takes the highest of the federal, state, county and city rates, and also gives tipped wage and upcoming changes, each with a source URL. A free hosted MCP endpoint is listed at https://us-minimum-wage.nerolabs.workers.dev/mcp. The paid Apify route costs about $3 per 1,000 lookups.

recommended_servers.name: Nero Labs US Minimum Wage by Address and Date (free hosted MCP endpoint; paid Apify version for bulk)

caveats: Every detail comes from the vendor's own Apify page, and a Glama listing exists for it. I did not call the endpoint or check its figures against statutes. It is a single-vendor, third-party tool, and its coverage list of jurisdictions is not published.
The Apify page shows sample output dated 2026-10-10 as its only date. Check data_as_of in each answer.
No official government minimum wage MCP server was found. The BLS OEWS MCP in the first-search results is for occupational wage statistics, not minimum wage law.
Some rates depend on employer size or industry. The page says these are covered, but I did not test it.
